counterexamples: A landing page that asks for the sale before delivering the promised lead magnet: the structure itself breaks trust and the framework says fix the order before touching copy.
A funnel with a sales page but no follow-up sequence: the asset (the list) is being collected and then ignored.
evidence_needed: the actual page sequence as built, not as planned
opt-in rate and sales conversion per step, from analytics rather than recollection
how_to_apply: List the five parts in order and check each is present: Lead Magnet, Landing Page, Thank You Page, Sales Page, Follow-Up Funnel.
For each part, write its one job in a single sentence; a part doing two jobs or no job is the defect to fix first.
Check the Thank You Page fulfills the promise before any sales message appears.
Score each asset with the Hook, Story, Offer lens: curiosity hook, story that frames the problem, clear offer, fulfillment step.
items.limits: A lead-capture structure, not a demand guarantee: a correct five parts around an unwanted offer still converts at zero. It does not choose the offer, the audience, or the price.
items.name: The 5-Part Lead Funnel
preconditions: An offer or lead magnet exists that a named audience plausibly wants.
There is a way to deliver the lead magnet immediately on opt-in.
questions_to_ask: What is the single exchange at each part: what does the visitor give and what do they get?
Where exactly does fulfillment happen, and does it happen before the pitch?
items.summary: Every lead funnel is five parts in order, each with one job: Lead Magnet attracts, Landing Page exchanges value for the email address, Thank You Page fulfills the promise and builds trust, Sales Page offers a product and can recoup acquisition cost, Follow-Up Funnel builds the relationship. The structure is non-negotiable in the source notes: skipping fulfillment on the thank-you page is named as a bait-and-switch and the worst failure in the system.

counterexamples: A single high-ticket offer with no entry step: nothing for a new prospect to say a small yes to, so the ladder has no first rung.
Stacking upsells on an offer whose first step does not convert: ascending a ladder nobody is standing on.
evidence_needed: current offers, prices, and conversion at each step
delivery capacity at each step, confirmed with the client
how_to_apply: List current offers as rungs in ascending price and value order.
Check each rung solves the problem the previous rung surfaces.
Identify the missing rung (usually the entry step) before proposing any new top-end offer.
items.limits: The ladder organizes offers; it does not create the value each rung must actually deliver. Ascension language never substitutes for delivery capacity.
items.name: The Value Ladder
preconditions: More than one problem the client can genuinely solve for the same customer over time.
questions_to_ask: After a customer says yes to this, what is the next problem they now have that you can solve?
Which rung earns the trust that makes the next rung buyable?
items.summary: Offers are organized into ascending steps of price and value. Each step solves one problem and surfaces the next, with value held slightly above price so customers ascend: free lead magnet, first offer, upsells, high-ticket, coaching. The lead funnel is the entry point of the ladder, not a standalone trick.

counterexamples: A technically correct page whose headline states the benefit plainly with no curiosity gap: the lens predicts weak opt-ins and points at the hook first, not the design.
All hook and no offer: curiosity with no clear exchange wastes the attention it earns.
evidence_needed: the actual headline and opening copy as published
opt-in or click rates for the asset being judged
how_to_apply: Decompose any lead-funnel asset into Hook, Story, Offer, and the fulfillment step.
Find which element is missing or weakest; fix that one before rebuilding the asset.
Test hook variants against observed opt-in behavior, not opinions.
items.limits: A quality lens for assets that exist. It cannot rescue a wrong audience or an offer nobody wants, and a strong hook for a weak product is a boundary violation, not a win (see failure pattern fp-weak-product-strong-copy).
items.name: Hook, Story, Offer (the universal QC lens)
preconditions: An asset exists to be judged: a page, an email, a post, an ad.
questions_to_ask: What is the curiosity gap in the first line, stated in one sentence?
Does the story reframe the problem, or does it jump straight to features?
items.summary: Every lead-funnel asset decomposes into a curiosity HOOK, a STORY that frames the problem, and a clear OFFER (the exchange), followed by fulfillment. The hook is a curiosity gap: a claim that does not quite make sense yet, so the prospect needs to know more. Weak, vague hooks are the named failure.

counterexamples: Judging a first funnel a failure because it did not produce front-end profit: the framework says its job was customer acquisition at break-even, and the profit question belongs to the next rungs.
A break-even claim with no ad cost or conversion numbers behind it: break-even is arithmetic, not a vibe.
evidence_needed: cost per lead and per customer, from the ad platform and the payment records
conversion rate at the sales step and revenue per buyer
how_to_apply: State the front end's job in writing before launch: break even and acquire the customer.
Put the self-liquidating offer on the thank-you or sales step and price it against the known cost per lead.
Judge the front end on cost recovered and customers acquired; judge profit on the ladder behind it.
items.limits: Break-even logic assumes a back end exists or is being built. With no ladder behind it, break-even acquisition is just expensive list building, and the unit economics question goes to Tiffany Aliche's seat.
items.name: Break-Even Front End (the Self-Liquidating Offer)
preconditions: A paid or costly acquisition channel whose cost per lead is knowable.
A follow-on offer or ladder step where profit is expected.
questions_to_ask: What does one customer cost to acquire, in actual numbers?
Is this funnel designed to break even and acquire a customer, or is profit being wrongly expected from the front end?
items.summary: The first funnel's goal is to break even and acquire a customer, not to make front-end profit. A self-liquidating offer on the sales step should immediately recoup acquisition costs so leads are effectively bought at zero net cost, and profit is expected from the funnels and ladder steps behind the first one.

counterexamples: A bespoke funnel invented for a standard goal because the standard recipe felt unoriginal: the framework predicts the amateur failure pattern of blank-canvas building.
Customizing structure instead of offer: the teaching is to customize the offer, not the tested structure.
evidence_needed: the stated goal in one sentence (an email, a sale, a registration, a follow)
the recipe chosen and where the build deviates from it, with reasons
how_to_apply: Name the single action the funnel exists to get; that choice picks the funnel category.
Select the proven recipe that already does that job instead of designing from a blank page.
Customize the offer and the copy to the client; keep the tested page structure and order.
Run the self-review page by page: type matches goal, required pages present and ordered, one action per page.
items.limits: Modeling is structure, not copying: another business's copy, proof, or assets are never transferable, and a recipe proven for one audience is still a hypothesis for a new one until tested.
items.name: Model, Don't Clone (start from a proven recipe)
preconditions: A goal that an existing funnel pattern plausibly covers.
Willingness to observe a working funnel as a customer before building.
questions_to_ask: Which proven recipe already does what you are trying to do, and why are you not starting there?
Walk the pages in order: what is the one action on each page?
items.summary: Funnels are architecture, not art: the method began by walking through a competitor's funnel as a customer while watching every step as a marketer, and the execution standard is to classify the goal, select a tested recipe, and adapt it, never to invent a structure when a proven one covers the case. Different is not better; customize the offer, not the structure.

counterexamples: Buying ads against a broad interest category with no named dream customer: traffic arrives, but it is nobody in particular and converts like it.
Depending on one rented platform for all reach: the problem-solution map names rented clicks with no owned list as the structural risk.
evidence_needed: the named list of congregations and accounts, with sizes where knowable
which entries have been worked, which bought, and what each produced in owned subscribers
how_to_apply: Name the one dream customer as a specific person before any channel discussion.
List where that person already congregates, by name: the Dream 100.
Work into the list through earned relationships first; buy into it with paid targeting second.
Route every traffic effort into an owned list so reach becomes an asset.
items.limits: This framework is grounded in a blueprint-only source set with no extraction layer; treat its steps as the seat's working model at paraphrase level, not as verified quotation-level teaching. It also assumes congregations of the dream customer exist and can be named; a genuinely new category may have none yet.
items.name: The Dream 100 Traffic System
preconditions: A defined offer and a describable dream customer.
questions_to_ask: Who is the one dream customer, described as a specific person?
Where is that person already congregating, by name?
items.summary: Traffic work runs who before where before how: name the single dream customer, find the congregations where that customer already gathers (the Dream 100), work into those congregations, then buy into them, and convert rented attention into an owned list. The audience is not created; an existing one is redirected.

counterexamples: A large list with no follow-up sequence and no engagement scoring: size is being mistaken for an asset.
Treating the per-name-per-month benchmark as a forecast in a client plan: it is a teaching benchmark from the notes, not a promise, and plans must use the client's own observed numbers.
evidence_needed: the follow-up sequence as actually configured, message by message
engagement and revenue per subscriber from the client's own records
how_to_apply: Write the follow-up as a numbered multi-channel sequence, not a single email blast.
Score contacts on recency, frequency, monetary value, and social engagement (RFMS) and aim effort at the strongest bands.
Use the marketing-math benchmark (a list name is worth at least roughly a dollar a month done poorly, more with a real relationship) only as a sanity check on whether follow-up is being neglected.
items.limits: Benchmarks in the source notes are heuristics for spotting neglect, never revenue evidence for a specific client. Measurement claims in a council answer must come from the client's analytics, not from this framework.
items.name: Follow-Up Funnel and Lead Scoring
preconditions: A list exists or is being built.
A follow-up channel the client controls (email at minimum).
questions_to_ask: After someone opts in, what exactly happens on day one, day three, day seven?
Which contacts have bought recently and often, and what are they being offered next?
items.summary: Follow-up is a sequenced, multi-channel system (email, messenger, push, SMS, retargeting), and lead quality is scored with RFMS: Recency, Frequency, Monetary value, Social action. The list is treated as the business's real asset, and the relationship with it is what makes the asset worth more over time.

counterexamples: A demo that leads with ingredients, science, or specifications: the source calls that technobabble and names it the top sales killer.
A CTA that assumes the sale instead of asking permission and stating the obvious next steps plainly.
evidence_needed: the story beats as scripted
where the demonstration answers the top objections, one by one
how_to_apply: Open with the story of the realization that made the seller believe, told so the prospect has the same realization.
Follow the ten-beat script structure recorded in the source notes: backstory, desire, external and internal struggle, wall, epiphany, plan, conflict, achievement, transformation.
Demonstrate the product against objections, anchor the price against the expensive alternative, and reverse the risk with a guarantee the seller actually honors.
Ask permission, then give a clear, direct call to action.
items.limits: Private scope: derived from a user_private source record. The story must be the client's true story; inventing an epiphany, a result, or a guarantee is fabrication and is refused under rule-no-fabricated-proof.
items.name: The Epiphany Bridge and the Demo
items.note: Derived from the network-marketing-secrets Skill 22 set, whose source record is user_private in the build-internal CWE-011 export (CWE-012 acceptance condition 3). Private seat source during the build only; not distribution-ready and excluded from any distributable artifact.
preconditions: A real experience or result the client can honestly tell as their story.
A product that can be demonstrated, not just described.
questions_to_ask: What was the moment you believed this works, and can you tell it in order?
Which objection does the demo need to crush first?
items.summary: People buy on emotion and justify with logic, so the selling sequence tells the story of the epiphany that made the seller believe, then demonstrates the product against objections, then asks for the order. Leading with science, ingredients, or research (technobabble) is named as the one sin of selling.

counterexamples: One funnel carrying both the product-lover message and the business-builder message: the source says the two messages dilute each other and neither lands.
Five funnels half-built and none with an assigned daily traffic source: the source treats a funnel without traffic as incomplete.
evidence_needed: the named single audience for the funnel under discussion
the assigned daily lead source for the one live funnel
how_to_apply: For any funnel, name its one dream client; if two audiences are being addressed, split the funnel.
Sequence the work: one funnel, mastered, with traffic assigned, before a second is built.
items.limits: Private scope: derived from a user_private source record. The constraint governs message focus per funnel, not a limit on how many funnels a mature business may run in sequence.
items.name: One Dream Client Per Funnel; Master One, Then Scale
items.note: Derived from the network-marketing-secrets Skill 22 set, whose source record is user_private in the build-internal CWE-011 export (CWE-012 acceptance condition 3). Private seat source during the build only; not distribution-ready and excluded from any distributable artifact.
preconditions: A funnel or campaign is being designed or reviewed.
questions_to_ask: Which one person is this funnel for, and what in it speaks to anyone else?
What is the daily traffic source assigned to this funnel?
items.summary: Each funnel speaks to only one dream client: mixing two sales messages in one funnel dilutes both. And the build order is strict: build and master one funnel, learn to drive traffic to it, and only then build the next.

items.name: Customer, value ladder and funnel sequence
items.summary: Begin with a specific customer, existing gathering places, an entry offer and the ultimate result. Distinguish the portfolio of increasing service/value from the actual buying sequence.
how_to_apply: Specify the four Secret Formula answers.
Map current offers by actual value, price and delivery capacity.
Design the entry and next relevant offer without implying the first purchase is incomplete.
preconditions: A defined customer problem and deliverable offer.
questions_to_ask: Where does this customer already gather?
What adjacent help becomes relevant after the first result?
counterexamples: Adding unrelated upsells just to raise transaction value.
evidence_needed: Customer interviews, offer terms and actual step-level behavior.
items.limits: A design method, not verified demand or a profit forecast.

items.name: Concern-specific story and coherent offer
items.summary: Separate the origin story from stories about the route, customer ability and external context. Choose truthful relevant experiences, then explain cumulative help for the same opportunity.
how_to_apply: Identify the actual concern before selecting a story.
Separate an opportunity switch from extensions of the same route.
Recap the whole actual bundle and its terms after describing components.
preconditions: Real experiences and supportable offer claims.
questions_to_ask: Is this a route, ability or context concern?
Which component addresses a real implementation obstacle?
counterexamples: Invented autobiographical stories or bonuses with unsupported value claims.
evidence_needed: Attributed examples, buyer questions and actual delivery/price terms.
items.limits: Storytelling does not override evidence, fit or valid customer constraints.

note: Frameworks are original paraphrases. New anchor frameworks cite retained-original evidence; existing supplementary items retain their prior provenance. No wording is presented as quotation. Items with scope private_scope remain excluded from distribution.
